boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Big Mound record (July 24-25, 1863) in Operations Against the Sioux in North Dakota [July 1863]. The march from Camp Pope and Camp Atchison and the return of the pursuing cavalry to camp on the morning of July 25 are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the District of Minnesota and the Santee and Teton Sioux without figures; the live field reads 0. Sibley says he had left a third of his force at Camp Atchison and moved with 1,400 infantry and 500 cavalry, and saw the whole body of Indians, 1,000 to 1,500, retiring. McPhaill says the Indians engaged could not have been less than 1,000 and would reach 1,500 warriors.
claims.rationale: The 1,400 and 500 describe the column one day's march beyond Camp Atchison as reported in Sibley's July 21 dispatch, before the action; the 1,000 to 1,500 are opponents' estimates of July 24. No account by the Dakota bands was inspected; their numbers, aims and losses come from their opponents' estimates, prisoners' or scouts' statements relayed by them, or the NPS summary. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

McPhaill says the ground was rocky and broken and his men dismounted to skirmish the hills.

claims.value: The frozen US commander is Brigadier General Henry Hastings Sibley. The frozen and live Native American commander is Inkpaduta (no rank; the live page tags him [CS], not adopted); none of the inspected reports names him, so his role is not established here. Sibley took a 6-pounder up the hill toward the Big Mound himself and directed McPhaill, Marshall and Crooks; McPhaill led the mounted charges and pursuit; Crooks drove back the threat on the left.
claims.rationale: Command roles from interested reports; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory; NPS says the Sioux forces were broken and dispirited. Sibley says the Indians fled in confusion and were chased at least 12 miles; McPhaill says his cavalry pursued about 15 miles. Sibley's troops burned the provisions and robes found at the abandoned camp on the 26th.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads US unknown and I 13; the live field reads 87 (US 7; CS 80). McPhaill says 31 Indians are known to have been killed by his regiment in the series of fights, and the compiler's note on his list shows 3 men killed and 4 wounded, including the skirmish of the 26th. Sibley gives, for the whole column in combat, 3 cavalrymen killed and 4 wounded, besides a man killed by lightning and Lieutenant Freeman killed while hunting; his figure of at least 150 Indians killed and wounded covers all three engagements.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. McPhaill's figures span July 24 and 26; Sibley's 150 is campaign context and is not assigned to this record.

open_questions: Marshall's and Baker's reports (Nos. 4-5), the appendix pages Sibley cites, the Dakota bands' own accounts, histories and maps remain deferred. McPhaill's report is the targeted follow-up for this record.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Sibley's August 7, 1863 report covers all three July engagements and is an interested account; Crooks's August 5 report (Sixth Minnesota) also covers all three and is a separate family. McPhaill's August 5, 1863 report (Mounted Rangers) is a separate family used as the follow-up. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.

No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Participants are named as the sources name them; characterizations in the sources (including 'hostile', 'savages', 'massacre' or 'battle') are quoted as the sources' own words and not adopted.
